report:
The argument establishes the requested restricted result: an infinite, explicitly specified, supremum-norm-bounded family of smooth normalized logarithmic densities has uniform positive upper and lower bounds for both exact-maximizer densities. Consequently, both critical L^(n/(n−1))(dV) estimates hold on the original fixed zero-lower-mass background.

I checked [Gauduchon’s primary article](https://www.numdam.org/article/AST_1985__126__129_0.pdf). Its general Theorem 2 applies; the even-Betti-number restriction belongs to Theorem 1. The Fredholm, sign and strict-positivity steps in its proof are valid. The different positive normalization of dd^c preserves the required zero equation. Every varying σ is smooth and strictly positive, so the theorem’s hypotheses hold.

The cofactor calculation is correct. Writing Q=σ^(n−1), one has n dd^cφ∧Q=J L_σφ dV and dQ=(n−1)dh∧σ^(n−2). The bilinear form defining A is real, symmetric and uniformly positive; its ellipticity bounds follow from δh≤σ≤Λh. The vector b is uniformly bounded because dQ contains no derivative of the varying Hessian. The displayed Stokes signs give P=div_dV(A d)−b·d and therefore div_dV(A dρ+bρ)=0. Absorbing the fixed coordinate volume density preserves these bounds.

The Harnack proof also closes without controlling div B. Testing by η²ρ^(p−1), for either sign of p−1, and applying Young’s inequality yields the stated power estimate. Sobolev applied to ηρ^(p/2) includes its ordinary additional cutoff term, giving an iteration factor bounded by C[1+p²(1+|p−1|^(−2))]. The chosen half-step geometric exponents stay a fixed distance from 1; the logarithms of the iteration constants grow at most linearly with the iteration index. Their weighted sum converges. Negative exponents give the corresponding estimate for ρ^(−1), without assuming a uniform lower bound beforehand.

The logarithmic test gives the claimed gradient bound. Scaling and cube Poincaré yield uniform BMO control. In the supplied dyadic construction, generation j has measure at most a^(−j)|Q| and accumulated oscillation at most (j2^m a+a)K₀. Choosing the exponential parameter sufficiently small makes the resulting geometric series converge. This bounds the product of the positive and negative p₀-moments and completes Harnack. A fixed connected finite chart cover gives a global constant H; the normalization ∫ρ dV=1 then gives H^(−1)≤ρ≤H. The cube Sobolev and Poincaré inequalities used here are routine consequences of one-dimensional integration and Hölder; no external Harnack or John–Nirenberg theorem is being assumed.

The exact-current normalization is correct with ordinary wedge powers. Stokes gives M₀=∫Jρ dV=∫h∧ρQ, so T*=ρQ/M₀ belongs to G_h and equals γ^(n−1), where γ=(ρ/M₀)^(1/(n−1))σ. The task’s smooth uniqueness identifies every exact maximizer with T*. Independently, matrix arithmetic–geometric mean and Stokes give D_Fv(T)≤c_v^(−1/n)∫σ_v∧T=c_v^(−1/n) for every test current; T* attains equality. Thus the construction concerns actual maximizers. The trace-normalized determinant calculation gives k_T*=J^(−1/n)r and dν/dV=r, with r=Jρ/M₀.

For the specified family, j₋≤J≤j₊ and j₋≤M₀≤j₊. Hence j₋/(Hj₊)≤r≤Hj₊/j₋, and multiplication by J^(−1/n) gives the asserted bounds for k_T*. Since dV is a probability volume, these upper bounds immediately give both critical norms. All constants depend only on the stated fixed geometry and ε₀.

The family assumptions and nonvacuity are established. The ratio J_v/J_h and its J_h-weighted average c_v/c_0 both lie between (1−ε₀)^n and (1+ε₀)^n, proving the stated supremum bound. Every F_v is smooth and normalized. For any smooth nonconstant φ, small multiples satisfy the Hessian restriction. The derivative of F_(tφ) at zero is L_hφ minus its J_h-weighted average. It is nonconstant: a constant L_hφ must vanish by evaluation at extrema, and the maximum principle would then force φ constant. A two-point difference is consequently strictly monotone on a small parameter interval, producing infinitely many distinct nonconstant normalized densities. Normalization excludes differences consisting merely of constant shifts.

The only harmless notation clarification is to call the variable mass c_v, rather than c_0, in the normalization section, reserving c_0 for v=0. No substantive repair is needed. The result applies to the specified Hessian-generated density family, not the whole bounded C⁰ ball, all Gauduchon tests, or near-maximizers. It neither implies positive lower mass for the full potential family nor establishes P16 singleton supports. External premises are indexed 0–2 below; passages marked −1 record task-granted background and are excluded from that list.

passages.statement: Every smooth positive Hermitian form σ on a connected compact complex manifold of complex dimension n≥2 admits a smooth positive function ρ, unique up to multiplication by a positive constant, satisfying dd^c(ρσ^(n−1))=0 (Gauduchon, Theorem 2).
